title: Local finite-flat lisse calculation for the evaluation Hom comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and write $F_S=\nu_S^*$ for comparison inverse image on ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Write $H_\tau=R\mathcal Hom_A$ on site $\tau$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $L$ be an etale locally constant sheaf with finite $A$-module stalks, all flat over $A$ (tensor with each stalk preserves exact sequences), regarded in degree zero. Let $N\in D^b_c(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

The evaluation-defined comparison of [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison]
$$\beta_{L,N}:F_SH_e(L,N)\longrightarrow H_p(F_SL,F_SN)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $L,N$. There exists an etale cover $\{U_i\to S\}$ trivializing $L$ by finite free modules. On any such cover, with chosen value $A^{r_i}$, restriction of this very map is the finite-free comparison $F_{U_i}(N|_{U_i})^{\oplus r_i}\to(F_{U_i}N|_{U_i})^{\oplus r_i}$ induced by evaluation. These restricted maps are identified through the localized-site internal-Hom isomorphisms, so the assertion includes compatibility on iterated restrictions and changes of trivialization. If $N$ has cohomology in $[u,v]$, then $H_e(L,N)$ has constructible cohomology in $[u,v]$, in particular it is bounded below. No finite-Tor condition on $N$ is imposed.

proof.text: The coefficient quotient is local: its defining positive power is contained in the maximal ideal of the valuation ring, so it is nontrivial and inherits locality by the surjective quotient map. Trivialize the lisse sheaf. On a nonempty cover member, its constant value is dualizable by the existing LisseDual theorem, hence finite and flat; the finite-flat local-ring theorem supplies a finite basis. On an empty member both sheaves are zero, and rank zero suffices.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs: finite-flat lisse first argument and evaluation comparison

proof.text: Construct a dual of L[0] by dualizing its single complex termwise. The existing bounded-complex duality gives the exact pairing after localization. Every dual term is lisse and dualizable, hence flat and constructible; GenericPerfect.constructibleFiniteTor_Q_obj_of_flat puts the dual in the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory. This is the private lisse_pairing proof, derived from the source-library APIs, without selecting an arbitrary object from an unproved existence theorem.

proof.text: For the canonical strong monoidal comparison inverse image, the evaluation-defined arrow is exactly ihomComparison. The exact pairing from the preceding step and isIso_ihomComparison_app_of_exactPairing make it invertible. Two-variable naturality follows from ihomComparison naturality and pre_naturality.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs: finite-flat lisse first argument and evaluation comparison

proof.text: Prove the finite-free coordinate assertion in closed monoidal categories whose right-tensor functors preserve finite coproducts. Under the tensor-Hom adjunction, maps to internal Hom correspond to maps out of K tensor T. Tensoring a colimiting finite cofan with T remains colimiting, so evaluation at its basis vectors induces a bijection on every Yoneda Hom set and hence an isomorphism to the finite product. A strong monoidal functor preserving finite coproducts carries the cofan to the unit-normalized mapped basis. Its evaluation comparison commutes with each coordinate by the tensorator naturality and unit law, yielding the exact stated piComparison equality. This includes rank zero and every choice of basis.

proof.text: Apply siteHomComparison_restriction on every etale object and again on every further etale object. Its conclusion is precisely the canonical evaluation-normalized restriction assertion required here; no alternative restriction maps are chosen.

proof.text: Identify RHom(L[0],N) with the derived tensor of the dual and N using the exact pairing. The source-library boundedConstructible_tensor theorem applies since the dual is bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude and N is merely bounded constructible. Transport along the tensor flip and Hom-tensor isomorphism, then use the constructible-sheaf comparison to obtain the statement's constructibility predicate and boundedness below. No finite-Tor assumption on N is introduced.

source.place: Second and third paragraphs: finite-flat lisse first argument and evaluation comparison

proof.text: Flatness gives Tor amplitude [0,0] for L[0]. The exact dual also has amplitude [0,0] by DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_of_exactPairing. The degreewise homology-tensor vanishing theorem therefore preserves each vanishing degree of N. Transfer this through ihomObjIsoTensor to obtain exactly the original interval, including the empty interval case.

There are no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from Q02's creation of the item, and it carries every argument of the parent's old step 7. The source is the master blueprint lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison, paragraphs 2-3. β is the evaluation transpose of def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison on ordinary constant-A modules on both sites, so the coefficient category is not substituted. Step checks: S1: A is finite local and L is lisse, and lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free (00NZ) makes each local value free; empty members and S empty are handled. S2: the slice square is upgraded to modules through the scalar endomorphisms; the RHom restriction η and the stated ev/tr equations of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose identify the restricted β. S3: the good truncation is written out; lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free applies with P'=A^r[0], needs no Tor condition, and ℓ is invertible on U_i. S4: the bounded-free model and the coordinate identification show the transpose is the tuple identity, with no sign. S5 (elementary): naturality, iterated restriction and local GL_r basis changes. S6: base-changed etale covers are pro-etale covers; the sheaf axiom kills H^t of the cone, and lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero concludes. S7: Hom(L,-) is exact, and D⊗G≅Hom(L,G) for every G. S8: H^t H_e ≅ D⊗H^t N, constructible by the tensor-refinement witness, which needs no flatness, giving the sharp [u,v]. Edge cases checked: L=0, N=0, S empty, and A=Z/4 with N=Z/2[0] (infinite Tor dimension). No cycle, no SGA, and all source tags exist with the stated labels. Tool uses are generic and accepted. The closure adds only Stacks 0951 (lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects), which the parent's old step 7 already reached. review_split's 'no such node' messages are a symlink artifact.
